original_value: Physical computing is a complex activity that consists of different but tightly coupled tasks: programming and assembling hardware for circuits. Prior work clearly shows that this coupling is the main source of mistakes that unfruitfully take a large portion of novices' debugging time. While past work presented systems that simplify prototyping or introduce novel debugging functionalities, these tools either limit what users can accomplish or are too complex for beginners. In this paper, we propose a general-purpose prototyping tool based on conversation. HeyTeddy guides users during hardware assembly by providing additional information on requests or by interactively presenting the assembly steps to build a circuit. Furthermore, the user can program and execute code in real-time on their Arduino platform without having to write any code, but instead by using commands triggered by voice or text via chat. Finally, the system also presents a set of test capabilities for enhancing debugging with custom and proactive unit tests. We codesigned the system with 10 users over 6 months and tested it with realistic physical computing tasks. With the result of two user studies, we show that conversational programming is feasible and that voice is a suitable alternative for programming simple logic and encouraging exploration. We also demonstrate that conversational programming with unit tests is effective in reducing development time and overall debugging problems while increasing users' confidence. Finally, we highlight limitations and future avenues of research.

result.paraphrase: Physical computing is a multifaceted activity involving tightly linked tasks such as circuit hardware assembly and programming. Prior work has shown that this interdependence is the primary cause of errors, which consume a large share of novices’ debugging time without producing useful results. Although previous systems have aimed to streamline prototyping or add new debugging features, they either constrain what users can do or are too complicated for beginners. In this paper, we introduce HeyTeddy, a general-purpose conversational prototyping tool. It supports hardware assembly by supplying extra information on demand and by interactively walking users through the steps needed to build a circuit. It also lets users program and run code on their Arduino platform in real time without writing code, instead using voice- or text-based chat commands. In addition, the system offers test features that improve debugging through custom and proactive unit tests. We co-designed the system with 10 users over 6 months and evaluated it on realistic physical computing tasks. Across two user studies, we show that conversational programming is feasible and that voice is a good alternative for implementing simple logic and supporting exploration. We also show that conversational programming with unit tests reduces development time and overall debugging issues while improving users’ confidence. Finally, we discuss limitations and directions for future research.
